day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary International Airport at 14:00. Take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~$60 CAD one-way, book in advance for best rates) to Banff town, approximately 1.5 hours. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge and freshen up. Take a relaxed walk along the Bow River Trail right in town to shake off travel fatigue and soak in your first mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll Banff Avenue to get oriented with the town. Visit the free Cascade Gardens viewpoint for a classic Banff townscape photo. Grab an early dinner and plan your week ahead.

meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or snacks at the Calgary Airport before boarding shuttle
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Bear Street - plant-forward, affordable bowls and wraps (~$15-18 CAD per person). Budget-friendly and filling after travel.

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before 14:00 arrival. Pick up a free Banff National Park trail map at the Banff Visitor Centre (224 Banff Ave) during your evening stroll - it opens until 5pm in summer. Note: A Parks Canada Discovery Pass is required to enter Banff National Park (~$72 CAD/person for an annual pass or ~$21 CAD/day). Purchase online or at the park gate to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Trail - Depart by 8:00am to beat the crowds. Drive or take the Roam Transit Bus Route 8X (~$6 CAD round trip) from Banff to Johnston Canyon, about 20 minutes away. Walk the iconic suspended catwalk trails carved into the canyon walls to reach the Lower Falls (1.1 km one-way) and Upper Falls (2.7 km one-way). The cool canyon air and rushing water make for a magical morning. Allow 2.5-3 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff town by early afternoon. Visit the free Banff Park Museum (free with Parks Pass) on Banff Ave for a quick cultural stop. Then hike up Tunnel Mountain Trail - a short but rewarding 2.3 km loop with panoramic views of the Bow Valley. Takes about 1-1.5 hours round trip.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the free Bow River viewpoint near the Bow Falls, a short walk from downtown. Enjoy the golden hour light on the Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and bagel from Whitebark Cafe or make your own at the lodge if kitchen facilities are available (~$8-10 CAD)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from the Safeway or IGA grocery store in Banff town the night before - sandwiches, fruit, and trail mix (~$8-10 CAD)
meals.dinner: Barpa Bill's Souvlaki on Bear Street - generous portions of Greek wraps and gyros for ~$14-16 CAD. One of Banff's best budget dinner spots.

day_by_day.notes: Start early at Johnston Canyon - by 9:30am the parking lot is full and trails get very crowded. Roam Transit is the most budget-friendly option. Wear layers as the canyon is noticeably cooler than town. Bring water and wear sturdy shoes as the catwalk can be slippery near the falls.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike - Depart Banff by 7:30am via Roam Transit Route 8X to Lake Louise (~$10 CAD round trip) or carpool/rideshare to save costs. Arrive early to see the iconic turquoise lake in calm morning light before crowds arrive. Walk the flat shoreline trail along the north shore of Lake Louise (3.5 km round trip, easy). Then begin the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail, continuing past the lake through subalpine meadows toward the historic teahouse (8.6 km round trip from the lake, moderate). The teahouse is a rewarding halfway milestone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse for a well-earned rest (~$8-12 CAD for tea and a baked good - cash only, budget accordingly). Enjoy views of the Victoria Glacier before heading back down. Return to Lake Louise village by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by bus. Rest tired legs back at the lodge. Optional: short walk to the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity grounds, which are free to wander and offer mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge or a quick oatmeal/granola bar before departure
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch from the grocery store the evening before - this is essential as Lake Louise village food is expensive. Eat at the picnic tables near the lakeshore (~$8-10 CAD self-packed)
meals.dinner: Melissa's Missteak on Lynx Street - a Banff institution with hearty burgers and pasta starting around $18-22 CAD. Slightly higher but worth it after a big hiking day.

day_by_day.notes: The Plain of Six Glaciers hike is approximately 14 km total with 365m elevation gain - wear proper hiking boots and bring trekking poles if available. The teahouse is cash only, so bring small bills. Lake Louise is one of the most visited spots in Canada - arriving before 8am makes a significant difference in experience. Check Roam Transit schedules the night before as Friday service may be busier.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive and Peyto Lake Viewpoint - Rent a car for the day if budget allows (~$60-80 CAD for a compact, split with travel companions to reduce cost) or join a budget group tour from Banff (~$50-70 CAD per person). Depart by 8:00am heading north on Highway 93 (Icefields Parkway). Stop at Bow Lake viewpoint (free, stunning turquoise glacial lake), then continue to the Bow Summit trailhead for the short 1.6 km hike up to Peyto Lake Viewpoint - one of the most photographed views in Canada, a wolf-shaped electric-blue lake surrounded by peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Weeping Wall viewpoint and Sunwapta Falls (short 0.5 km walk, included with Parks Pass). If budget allows, stop at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre to view the Athabasca Glacier from the free roadside viewpoint (note: glacier walk tours are expensive at ~$100+ CAD and are optional). Begin the scenic drive back south along the Parkway, stopping at Mistaya Canyon (0.8 km easy walk) for a dramatic limestone gorge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by 6:00-7:00pm. Enjoy a quiet evening on Banff Avenue. Visit the free Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies courtyard area.

meals.breakfast: Pack a hearty breakfast from the grocery store - bagels with peanut butter, fruit, and coffee in a thermos to eat on the road
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch eaten at Bow Lake or Peyto Lake picnic areas - sandwiches, cheese, crackers, and trail mix (~$10-12 CAD self-packed). This is critical as there are very few affordable food options along the Parkway.
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's on Bear Street - Cajun-inspired comfort food with generous portions and mains around $16-20 CAD. A great budget-friendly dinner after a long driving day.

day_by_day.notes: The Icefields Parkway is 230 km one-way to the Columbia Icefield - plan which stops matter most to you and don't try to do everything. Fill up your gas tank in Banff before departing as fuel on the Parkway is very limited and expensive. Bring plenty of water and snacks. Wildlife sightings (elk, bears, bighorn sheep) are common along the Parkway - always maintain safe distances and never feed animals. Saturday can be very busy at Peyto Lake - arrive at the trailhead by 9am.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Hike (budget alternative to the Gondola) - Instead of paying ~$60 CAD for the Banff Gondola, hike up the Sulphur Mountain Trail (5.5 km one-way, 655m elevation gain, strenuous). The trail starts at the Upper Hot Springs parking area, a short walk or free shuttle from town. Allow 2-3 hours to summit. At the top, enjoy 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges and the Bow Valley. The boardwalk and interpretive signs at the summit are free to access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Sulphur Mountain (or take the Gondola down for ~$30 CAD if legs are tired). Stop at the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$16.50 CAD adult admission) for a well-deserved soak in the naturally heated mineral pool with mountain views - a quintessential Banff experience and very affordable. Towel rental is available (~$2 CAD) if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Back in town, browse the free art galleries along Banff Avenue. Catch sunset from the Bow River bridge near Bow Falls for stunning alpenglow on Mount Rundle.

meals.breakfast: Grocery store supplies - make oatmeal with fruit at the lodge or grab a hearty muffin and coffee from a local bakery (~$6-8 CAD)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the Sulphur Mountain summit or base - pack wraps, cheese, and energy bars from the grocery store (~$8-10 CAD)
meals.dinner: Masala Authentic Indian Cuisine on Caribou Street - generous portions of curry and naan for ~$16-20 CAD, great value and very filling after an active day.

day_by_day.notes: The Sulphur Mountain hike saves you ~$30 CAD compared to the full Gondola round-trip while providing the same summit experience. Start the hike by 8:00am to avoid midday heat and afternoon crowds. Bring sunscreen as the upper trail and summit boardwalk are exposed. The Upper Hot Springs complex has lockers for a small fee. Swimwear is required at the hot springs - pack yours from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Vermilion Lakes Morning Walk - Start your final morning with a peaceful, flat 5 km walk along the Vermilion Lakes Road, just minutes from downtown Banff. These shallow lakes offer stunning reflections of Mount Rundle and are prime wildlife habitat - watch for beavers, herons, and possibly elk in the early morning. This is one of the best free experiences in Banff and perfect for photography. Allow 1.5-2 hours at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon exploring any remaining Banff town highlights. Visit the Luxton Museum of the Plains Indian (small admission ~$10 CAD) or browse the free Banff Park Museum. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping along Banff Avenue - look for affordable gifts at the Banff Trading Post or Rocky Mountain Soap Company. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Banff via Banff Airporter shuttle back to Calgary International Airport (book in advance, ~$60 CAD). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the drive and airport check-in. Enjoy one last look at the Rockies on the drive back to Calgary.

meals.breakfast: Cows Ice Cream and Cafe or Wild Flour Bakery on Bear Street for a fresh pastry and coffee send-off (~$10-12 CAD) - treat yourself on your last morning!
meals.lunch: Subway or a grocery store grab-and-go meal near Banff Ave for a quick, affordable lunch before packing up (~$10-12 CAD)
meals.dinner: Airport food or pack leftover snacks for the journey home - save your remaining budget for the road.

day_by_day.notes: Book your return Banff Airporter shuttle at least 24 hours in advance to guarantee your seat. Vermilion Lakes is a 10-minute walk or free bike ride from the Banff town centre. If you have a late evening flight, you can extend your afternoon activities. Leave no trace in all natural areas visited - pack out all garbage. Consider purchasing a reusable Parks Canada map as a lasting souvenir (~$5 CAD at the Visitor Centre).

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary International Airport at 14:00. Collect luggage and rent a car (recommended for the trip). Drive approximately 1.5 hours west on the Trans-Canada Highway to Banff. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along Banff Avenue to get oriented — browse local shops and soak in the mountain town atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Banff on foot. Visit Cascade Gardens for a peaceful introductory view of Cascade Mountain. Head to dinner and wind down after travel.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a meal on the plane or grab a quick bite at Calgary Airport (Tim Hortons or Freshii)
meals.lunch: Grab a casual bite en route — stop at a gas station deli or fast-casual spot in Canmore (e.g., Communitea Café)
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace in Banff — locally sourced Canadian cuisine with mountain views; mid-range pricing around CAD $35–55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Do not schedule strenuous activities on arrival day. Pick up a Parks Canada day pass or annual Discovery Pass at the park gate on the way in — required for all park access. Confirm car rental has a roof rack or space for hiking gear.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Trail — depart the hotel by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Follow the suspended catwalk trails carved into the canyon walls to reach the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). The cool canyon air makes this a perfect morning hike. Allow approximately 2.5–3 hours round trip. Wear sturdy shoes as the catwalks can be slippery.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, drive back toward Banff (Johnston Canyon is ~20 min west of town). Stop at Vermilion Lakes on the way back for a scenic lakeside walk and excellent wildlife-spotting opportunities — elk and beaver are commonly seen here. Spend the afternoon relaxing by the lakes or renting a canoe at the Banff Canoe Club on the Bow River (approx. CAD $60/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh. Head into downtown Banff for dinner and an evening walk along the Bow River pathway.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab coffee and pastries at Wild Flour Bakery Café in Banff before departing
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch — pick up sandwiches and snacks the night before from Nesters Market in Banff
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tooloulou's Restaurant in Banff — relaxed Cajun-inspired menu, great value, mains around CAD $20–35

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon parking fills up extremely fast — arrive before 8:30 AM or take the Banff Transit Roam Bus Route 8X (Bow Valley Parkway route) to avoid parking stress. Bring a light jacket as the canyon is noticeably cooler than outside.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake and Valley of the Ten Peaks — this is the most in-demand destination in Banff, so depart by 6:00 AM. Private vehicles require a timed-entry reservation (book via Parks Canada in advance). Walk the Rockpile Trail (20 min) for the iconic panoramic viewpoint over the vivid blue-green lake framed by the ten peaks. Then hike the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km round trip, easy) for close-up views of the glacially fed waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive approximately 14 km to Lake Louise. Walk the Lake Louise Shoreline and begin the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail — hike past the teahouse at 5.3 km (one way) for stunning glacier views and a well-earned tea and scone break. The full return hike is approximately 13.8 km with 365 m elevation gain; moderate difficulty. Allow 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Banff (45 min). Relax at the hotel. Enjoy a sit-down dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Early morning — grab pre-packed granola bars, fruit, and a thermos of coffee from the hotel or Nesters Market the evening before
meals.lunch: Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse at the trail — soups, sandwiches, and baked goods; cash only, mid-range pricing (~CAD $15–25); a truly memorable lunch spot
meals.dinner: Dinner at Coyotes Southwestern Grill in Banff — vibrant flavours, vegetarian-friendly options, mains CAD $22–38

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake timed-entry reservations are mandatory and sell out months in advance — book as early as possible via the Parks Canada reservation system. Alternatively, use the Parks Canada Shuttle from Lake Louise overflow parking. Carry bear spray (rentable in Banff) and make noise on trails. Both lakes are at high elevation — bring layers even in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola and Summit Hike — take the Banff Gondola (book tickets online in advance, approx. CAD $65–75/person) to the summit at 2,281 metres for sweeping 360-degree views of six mountain ranges. Walk the Sulphur Mountain Boardwalk Ridge (1 km) to the historic Sanson's Peak meteorological station. Alternatively, hike up the Sulphur Mountain Trail (5.5 km one way, 655 m elevation gain) to earn your gondola ride down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and head to the Banff Upper Hot Springs (approx. CAD $16–20/person) located at the base of Sulphur Mountain — a perfect recovery soak with mountain views. Spend 1.5–2 hours relaxing in the mineral-rich waters. Return to the hotel to rest.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Banff. Browse the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (open until 5 PM — adjust if needed) or simply walk along the Bow River. Treat yourself to a nicer dinner tonight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Evelyn's Coffee Bar in Banff — cozy, local favourite with great espresso and breakfast sandwiches
meals.lunch: Sky Bistro at the Gondola summit — panoramic dining experience, mid-range to slightly upscale; mains CAD $28–45; worth it for the views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Park Distillery Restaurant + Bar — locally distilled spirits and hearty Canadian fare; mains CAD $25–45; lively atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Booking the gondola online in advance saves time and often money. The hike up Sulphur Mountain is a rewarding alternative for fit hikers and takes approximately 2 hours up. Hot Springs towel rentals are available on-site. This is a great recovery day balancing activity with relaxation.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive — depart Banff by 8:00 AM for one of the world's most spectacular drives. Head north on Highway 93 toward Jasper. First major stop: Bow Lake (approx. 1 hour from Banff) — short lakeside walk with stunning reflections of Crowfoot Glacier. Continue to Peyto Lake Viewpoint — a short 1 km uphill walk to a breathtaking overlook of the wolf-shaped electric-blue lake surrounded by forest and peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Columbia Icefield area (approx. 2.5 hours from Banff). Visit the Athabasca Glacier — walk to the toe of the glacier on your own (free) or book an Ice Explorer tour (approx. CAD $60–80/person). Stop at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre for exhibits on glaciology. Begin the return drive south along the Parkway — stop at Sunwapta Falls or Athabasca Falls if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by 7:00–8:00 PM. Grab a casual dinner and reflect on the day's extraordinary scenery.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure, or coffee and muffins from a Banff café to go
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at Peyto Lake or Bow Lake — pick up supplies from Nesters Market the evening before (sandwiches, fruit, trail mix)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Melissa's Missteak in Banff — a beloved local institution known for hearty burgers, steaks, and casual atmosphere; mains CAD $20–40

day_by_day.notes: Fill up your gas tank in Banff before departing — there are very few fuel stations along the Icefields Parkway. Bring layers as temperatures at the Columbia Icefield are significantly colder (can feel like 10°C even in July). Wildlife sightings (bears, elk, bighorn sheep) are common along this route — keep a safe distance and never feed animals. The full Banff-to-Columbia Icefield-and-back drive is approximately 4–5 hours of driving total.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final relaxed morning in Banff. Take a peaceful sunrise walk to the Bow Falls viewpoint (10-minute walk from downtown) — a beautiful and easy farewell to the Rockies. Return for a proper sit-down breakfast. Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge (standard checkout 11:00 AM — confirm with hotel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Calgary International Airport (approximately 1.5 hours). Allow extra time for car rental return and airport check-in. Enjoy a final browse of the Banff Avenue shops before departing if time permits, or stop in Canmore for a last coffee and souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Calgary International Airport. Carry fond memories of the Canadian Rockies.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Whitebark Café in Banff — excellent eggs Benedict, locally roasted coffee, and a warm mountain atmosphere; budget CAD $18–28
meals.lunch: Grab lunch at The Communitea Café in Canmore en route to Calgary, or a quick meal at the Calgary Airport
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining at Calgary International Airport (various options available in the terminal)

day_by_day.notes: Return any rented gear (bear spray, hiking poles) before leaving Banff. Keep your Parks Canada pass handy until you exit the park gate. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the drive, car return, and check-in. Consider picking up local souvenirs at Banff Trading Post or Rocky Mountain Soap Company before departing.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight AC arrives at 14:00. Travel time from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge is approximately 1.5 hours by private transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Calgary Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge. Check in, unpack, and settle into your suite. Take a leisurely stroll along the Bow River Promenade in downtown Banff to stretch your legs and soak in the mountain atmosphere. Browse the boutiques on Banff Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the hotel or a short walk to one of Banff's finest restaurants. Toast to the start of your alpine adventure with a glass of Canadian wine on a scenic patio.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast on the plane or grab a snack at Calgary Airport.
meals.lunch: Light meal at Calgary Airport or en route — consider picking up provisions at a gourmet deli in Calgary before the transfer.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Maple Leaf Restaurant in downtown Banff — a celebrated fine-dining institution specializing in premium Canadian cuisine including Alberta bison, wild salmon, and locally foraged ingredients. Excellent wine cellar and warm mountain ambiance.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (e.g., Brewster Express private car or a local limousine service) from Calgary Airport for a seamless arrival. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. The Banff Mountain Lodge is within easy walking distance of downtown Banff.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola and Summit Hike — Board the Banff Gondola for a breathtaking ride to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres. Arrive early (gondola opens at 8:00 AM) to beat crowds and enjoy crystal-clear morning light over the Bow Valley. Walk the 1 km summit boardwalk to Sanson Peak, explore the interpretive centre, and take in 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by gondola and head to the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a premium soak in the naturally heated mineral waters at 1,585 metres elevation — a perfect way to relax muscles after the morning walk. Afterward, enjoy a private guided walking tour of the historic Cave and Basin National Historic Site, the birthplace of Canada's national park system.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant dinner at Castello Ristorante or Eden at the Rimrock Resort Hotel — one of Banff's most acclaimed fine-dining destinations offering modern European cuisine with impeccable mountain views. Reserve a window table for sunset over the Bow Valley.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge — fuel up well before the gondola ride.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Sky Bistro at the summit of Sulphur Mountain — Banff's highest-elevation restaurant offering elevated Canadian cuisine with panoramic mountain views. The prix-fixe lunch menu is highly recommended.
meals.dinner: Eden Restaurant at the Rimrock Resort Hotel — award-winning fine dining featuring a tasting menu with wine pairings, showcasing premium Canadian ingredients in an intimate, luxurious setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sky Bistro and Eden Restaurant reservations well in advance. Gondola tickets can be pre-purchased online to skip queues. Bring layers — summit temperatures can be 5–8°C cooler than town even in summer. The hot springs towel and locker rental is available on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Shoreline Hike — Depart early by private car or luxury shuttle to Lake Louise (approximately 45 minutes from Banff). Begin the iconic shoreline walk along the impossibly turquoise glacial lake with the Victoria Glacier as a backdrop. Continue on the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail (14 km round trip, moderate difficulty) through ancient moraines and alpine meadows, ascending to the historic Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse perched at 2,135 metres.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a well-earned rest and light refreshments at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse — a legendary alpine hut serving homemade soups, sandwiches, and baked goods entirely without electricity. Descend back to Lake Louise at a leisurely pace, pausing for photography. Visit the iconic Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise for afternoon tea in the Lakeview Lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise — choose from the Walliser Stube Wine Bar and Restaurant for a cozy Swiss-inspired fondue and raclette experience, or the elegant Fairview Bar and Restaurant for refined Canadian cuisine overlooking the lake at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge before departure — request a packed gourmet trail lunch from the hotel kitchen the evening prior.
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed trail lunch from the hotel plus hot drinks and baked goods at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (cash only at the teahouse — bring Canadian dollars).
meals.dinner: Walliser Stube at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise — intimate Swiss-alpine atmosphere with premium fondue, Swiss cheese specialties, and an exceptional wine list. A truly memorable mountain dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Start by 7:30–8:00 AM to secure parking at Lake Louise or arrange a private driver to drop off and collect. The Plain of Six Glaciers hike is 14 km round trip with 365 m elevation gain — wear sturdy hiking boots and bring trekking poles. Wildlife sightings (bears, pikas, marmots) are common — carry bear spray. The teahouse is cash only. Book Fairmont dinner reservations in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake and Valley of the Ten Peaks — Depart very early (6:00–6:30 AM) as Moraine Lake Road requires a Parks Canada shuttle reservation or private vehicle and fills up extremely fast in summer. Hike the Rockpile Trail for the iconic Valley of the Ten Peaks panorama at sunrise — one of the most photographed views in Canada. Continue on the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km, easy) for intimate turquoise lake views, then ascend the more challenging Consolation Lakes Trail (5.8 km round trip) for solitude and stunning alpine scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by midday. Enjoy a relaxed afternoon with a private guided interpretive nature walk along the Fenland Trail or Vermilion Lakes, where you can observe beaver dams, waterfowl, and possibly elk or deer in a serene wetland setting. Alternatively, indulge in a luxury spa treatment at the Banff Mountain Lodge or a nearby world-class spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at the Banff Springs Hotel's Rundle Bar with sweeping views of the Bow Valley, followed by a premium dinner at the Banff Springs Hotel's 1888 Chop House — a legendary steakhouse serving prime Alberta beef aged in-house, with an extensive cellar of rare Canadian and international wines.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast or packed breakfast from the hotel before 6:00 AM departure — request this from the hotel the evening before.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch with gourmet provisions prepared by the hotel, enjoyed at the shores of Moraine Lake or Consolation Lakes.
meals.dinner: 1888 Chop House at the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel — iconic fine dining in a castle-like setting. Prime Alberta beef, fresh seafood tower, and sommelier-curated wine pairings. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake Road access is strictly managed by Parks Canada in summer. Book the Parks Canada shuttle from Lake Louise Ski Area in advance at reservation.pc.gc.ca — these sell out weeks ahead. Alternatively, arrange a licensed private tour operator with access. Bring bear spray, layers, and arrive at the shuttle point by 5:30 AM. This is the most logistically demanding day — confirm all bookings before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive and Peyto Lake Viewpoint — Embark on a full-day private luxury drive along the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93), widely regarded as one of the most spectacular highways on Earth. First major stop: Bow Lake and Num-Ti-Jah Lodge for a short lakeside walk. Continue to the Bow Summit for the iconic hike to Peyto Lake Viewpoint (2.7 km round trip, easy-moderate) — the wolf-shaped turquoise lake surrounded by glaciers and forest is one of Canada's most spectacular vistas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north on the Icefields Parkway to the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre. Board the Ice Explorer — a massive all-terrain vehicle — for a guided excursion onto the Athabasca Glacier, one of the most accessible glaciers in North America. Walk on ancient glacial ice and hear expert commentary on climate and geology. Visit the Glacier Skywalk, a glass-floored observation platform suspended 280 metres above the Sunwapta Valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return south along the Parkway, stopping at Sunwapta Falls and Athabasca Falls for dramatic waterfall photography in the golden evening light. Arrive back in Banff for a late but well-deserved dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge before an early 7:30 AM departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Num-Ti-Jah Lodge dining room on the shores of Bow Lake — a historic backcountry lodge serving hearty Canadian fare with unbeatable lake and glacier views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse in downtown Banff — a premium steakhouse known for AAA Alberta beef, creative cocktails, and a lively yet refined atmosphere. Perfect for a celebratory end to a spectacular day.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private driver or luxury tour operator for the Icefields Parkway day — driving yourself means you can't fully enjoy the views. Recommended operators include Pursuit Banff Jasper Collection. Book Ice Explorer and Glacier Skywalk tickets in advance online. The full day is approximately 10–12 hours — bring layers as the Columbia Icefield area is significantly colder (can be near 0°C on the glacier). Carry snacks and water.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Trail — A perfect final morning activity close to Banff (25 minutes by car). Walk the suspended catwalk trails carved dramatically into the canyon walls to the Lower Falls (2.4 km round trip, easy) and Upper Falls (5.4 km round trip, moderate). The canyon is magical in morning light with mist rising from the turquoise pools. Continue optionally to the Ink Pots — seven cold mineral springs in an open alpine meadow (11.6 km round trip total) — or turn back at the Upper Falls for a shorter outing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff for a leisurely final afternoon. Treat yourself to a premium spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa. Explore Banff Avenue for last-minute shopping — look for Canadian-made goods, Indigenous art, and artisan souvenirs. Visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for a cultural send-off celebrating the art and history of the region.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the Banff Mountain Lodge or your preferred restaurant. Celebrate the end of a magnificent trip with a special tasting menu and wine pairing. Pack bags and arrange private transfer to Calgary Airport for the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge — savour it slowly before your last morning hike.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Johnston Canyon Resort's Trailhead Kitchen, or pack a gourmet picnic to enjoy beside the canyon.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Chez François or the Bison Restaurant and Terrace in downtown Banff — the Bison is celebrated for its locally sourced, farm-to-table Canadian cuisine including wild bison, Alberta lamb, and house-made charcuterie, with a warm rustic-luxe atmosphere perfect for a memorable final evening.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon can be busy by mid-morning — aim to arrive by 8:00 AM. Wear non-slip footwear as the catwalk can be wet and slippery near the falls. Confirm checkout time with Banff Mountain Lodge and arrange luggage storage if needed for the afternoon. Book private transfer to Calgary Airport in advance — allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight departure. A perfect trip — the Canadian Rockies will leave a lasting impression.
